original.target_description: Experiment 2: effect of assigned search condition on patient choices across all trials; hierarchical logistic regression.

n.sample_role: participants; choices analyzed hierarchically across all trials
n.exclusions: Primary replication report states 37 participants excluded for attending to no information on more than 20% of trials; dominated choices on both catch trials excluded; trials with no information review excluded.
n.quote: We recruited 207 participants (87 women; mean age, 34.3 y) via Amazon Mechanical Turk.

replication.target_description: Hypothesis to replicate and bet on: Comparative searchers make more patient choices (i.e., choose a larger monetary reward which is delivered later) than integrative searchers. The authors test the above hypothesis in a hierarchical logistic regression (β = –0.23, SE = 0.10, p = 0.027); pp. 11892–11893.

n.exclusions: Since the experiment was expected to take an average of 10 minutes, we had a show-up fee of $1.5. Note that the analysis code provided by the authors only covered the main analysis but not the data preprocessing. We used the same preprocessing procedure as described in the original manuscript. However, the code itself was written by the replication team and should not be considered formally preregistered. The original authors disagreed about the exact steps in preprocessing the replication data and sent us the code for their preferred preprocessing of the replication data (and the replication results based on their preferred preprocessing). The original authors’ preferred preprocessing resulted in more exclusions of observations and a sample size of n = 857, but the replication result based on their preferred preprocessing is similar to our reported replication results (the result based on the preprocessing preferred by the original authors (based on the original authors’ estimation) is: b = –0.069, se = 0.062; z = 1.111, p = 0.267, d = 0.076, 95% CI [−0.058, 0.210]; our reported replication result is: b = –0.051, se = 0.047; z = 1.084, p = 0.278, d = 0.067, 95% CI [−0.054, 0.188]). It should be noted that the data preprocessing in this study was complicated due to ambiguity about the exact preprocessing steps in the original paper (as we did not have access to the raw data or the preprocessing code used in the original study).
